MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted name] Medical Center
Department of Clinical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Name: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]
Sex: Male
Specimen Type: Peripheral Blood
Collection Date: [redacted date]
Received Date: [redacted date]
Report Date: [redacted date]

REFERRAL INFORMATION
Referring Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Clinical Indication: Diagnostic testing for suspected infertility, query Cystic Fibrosis as underlying cause

TEST PERFORMED
CFTR Gene Sequencing - Targeted Panel

METHODOLOGY
Targeted next-generation sequencing of the CFTR gene (NM_000492.4) was performed, analyzing:
• Exons 4, 6a, 7, 10-13, 19-21
• Part of intron 19
• Intron 8 polyT/polyTG tract regions

This panel provides coverage of variants representing:
• 87.65% of pathogenic variants in Caucasian populations
• 56.41% of pathogenic variants in South Asian populations
• 76% of pathogenic variants worldwide

DNA was extracted from peripheral blood using standard protocols. Library preparation was performed using targeted amplicon-based enrichment, followed by sequencing on an Illumina platform. Minimum coverage depth of 100x was achieved for all targeted regions. Variant calling and annotation were performed using validated bioinformatics pipelines.

RESULTS

CFTR Gene Analysis:

Variant 1 (Allele 1):
• Location: Intron 8
• Genotype: c.1210-12T(5) with c.1210-34TG(12)
• Description: 5T allele with 12TG repeats on the same chromosome
• Zygosity: Heterozygous
• Classification: Variant of uncertain significance

Variant 2 (Allele 2):
• Location: Intron 8
• Genotype: c.1210-12T(7) with c.1210-34TG(10)
• Description: 7T allele with 10TG repeats
• Zygosity: Present on second allele
• Classification: Normal variant

No other pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants were detected in the analyzed regions of the CFTR gene.

INTERPRETATION

The patient is heterozygous for the intron 8 5T allele in combination with 12TG repeats on the same chromosome. The 5T variant reduces the efficiency of CFTR exon 9 splicing, leading to decreased levels of functional CFTR protein. The presence of 12TG repeats (as opposed to 10TG or 11TG) is associated with greater penetrance of CFTR-related symptoms when found with the 5T allele.

The 5T/12TG genotype has been associated with:
• Congenital bilateral absence of vas deferens (CBAVD) when present with a severe CFTR mutation on the opposite allele
• Atypical CF or CFTR-related disorders in some cases
• Variable penetrance and expressivity

Population frequency of 5T allele: ~5% in general population
Population frequency of 5T/12TG combination: ~1-2% in general population

CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE

The 5T/12TG genotype identified in this patient, without a second identifiable CF-causing variant, is unlikely to be the sole cause of infertility. However, if CBAVD is confirmed clinically, the patient's infertility may be due to CFTR-related disease, possibly involving other rare or undefined variants not covered by this targeted panel.

It is important to note that:
1. This targeted panel covers approximately 76% of worldwide CF variants
2. Deep intronic variants, large deletions/duplications, and regulatory region variants are not assessed by this test
3. The clinical phenotype can be influenced by genetic modifiers and environmental factors

RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Clinical correlation is essential. If CBAVD diagnosis is confirmed through clinical examination and imaging:
   • Consider comprehensive CFTR variant screening at a specialist CF laboratory
   • This may include full gene sequencing, deletion/duplication analysis, and deep intronic variant assessment

2. Genetic counseling is recommended to discuss:
   • Implications for family planning
   • Risk assessment for future offspring
   • Testing options for the patient's partner

3. Consider evaluation for other subclinical CFTR-related manifestations

LIMITATIONS
• This test does not detect all possible CFTR variants
• Large deletions/duplications are not assessed
• Variants in non-coding regions (except specified intronic regions) are not evaluated
• Rare variants may not be detected due to technical limitations

This test was developed and validated by [redacted name] Medical Center Molecular Genetics Laboratory. The laboratory is certified under Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) and accredited by the College of American Pathologists (CAP).

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
